display.purpose: KPI metric values on the dashboard. The largest in-app text. Never in running copy.

headline.purpose: Page titles and dashboard welcome header. One per page.

title.purpose: Card section headers, modal titles, sidebar section headings.

body.purpose: All standard UI text, table cell content, form labels. Max 65-75ch in reading contexts.

label.purpose: Table column headers, nav section dividers, badge text. Always uppercase with 0.05em tracking.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Card hover lift. Signals interactivity; not used at rest.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: Modal. The only large shadow in the system; communicates interruption.

shadows.name: button-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover only. Reinforces Signal Blue identity on the primary action.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for all state changes: hover, focus, active. Snappy.

motion.name: panel-slide
motion.purpose: Sidebar mobile open/close. Slightly slower to feel physical.

motion.name: entrance-stagger
motion.purpose: Dashboard KPI cards on page load only. Staggered 90ms between cards. Never on routine navigation.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column table columns appear; filter row wraps less.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar becomes fixed (not overlay). Third table column appears.

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.overview:
Wareflow is designed around a single metaphor: a well-kept logbook. Every number is accurate. Every action is traceable. The interface never calls attention to itself; it calls attention to the data.

The visual language is a single sans family (Plus Jakarta Sans) at tightly-controlled weights, a cool near-white field, and a single accent color so precise in its placement that it feels authoritative the moment it appears. Signal Blue (#004ac6) is not a decoration; it is a directive.

This system explicitly rejects two traps: the bloated enterprise (heavy sidebars, 20-column tables, nested modals) and the over-animated startup (skeleton loaders on every panel, entrance choreography on routine navigation).
keyCharacteristics: Single sans typeface; hierarchy through weight and size, not family switching.
Restrained color: Signal Blue occupies less than 10% of any screen.
Flat surfaces by default; depth through tonal layers, not shadows.
Tables for operations data. Cards for summaries and KPIs only.
Motion limited to state transitions (150-200ms ease-out).
Full dark mode via CSS class toggle with blue-shifted neutrals.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue (#004ac6) is used as a fill on less than 10% of any screen. Its scarcity is its authority.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Error Red is reserved for genuine error states and destructive confirmations. Never for decoration.

rules.name: The Weight Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is achieved through weight contrast (400 to 700) and size steps with at least a 1.25 ratio.

rules.name: The Mono Exception Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for machine-readable strings: SKUs, reference codes, timestamps. Never for decorative copy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, modal).

rules.name: The Table Rule
rules.body: Operations data belongs in tables, not cards. Cards communicate summaries; tables communicate operations.

dos: Do use Signal Blue only for the primary action, active navigation state, focus rings, and interactive link text.
Do use tonal surface layers (Card White on Work Surface, Surface Low in table headers) to create depth.
Do use tables for inventory, stock movements, user lists, and warehouse data.
Do use Label-tier typography (11px / 600 / uppercase) for all table headers and navigation section dividers.
Do keep motion to state transitions (150-200ms ease-out). Entrance animations on page-load only.
Do pair every color-only state signal with a text or icon secondary indicator.
donts: Don't build nested navigation, collapsible sub-menus, or multi-level breadcrumbs. Never feel like SAP.
Don't add skeleton loaders or loading placeholders on routine page transitions.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Signal Blue is a solid color.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or alerts.
Don't stack shadows. One shadow level per z-index layer.
Don't show a disabled button where hiding it would better communicate the constraint.
Don't use identical card grids for list data. Use tables or varied layouts instead.
Don't open a modal as the first response to a user action if an inline approach exists.
